scenario_prompt: Write a two-paragraph executive summary addressed directly to a fictional buyer's Chief Financial Officer, recommending a cloud migration. Context: a mid-market freight brokerage firm is moving its load-matching and carrier-settlement systems off on-premises Microsoft SQL Server (28 instances) running on Hyper-V (620 virtual machines) onto Google Cloud, targeting Google Compute Engine for compute and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer, over a 2-year, $4,200,000 programme. The CFO has stated she is measured on reducing the current $1,850,000 annual technology spend and on a clean DOT compliance audit, which opens in 6 months. Cover why this matters to her now and what she should expect from the programme. Return only the summary text, two paragraphs, no headers.
text:
Executive summary

Diane, your $1,850,000 annual technology spend is anchored by 28 Microsoft SQL Server instances running across 620 Hyper-V virtual machines on premises, supporting the load-matching and carrier-settlement systems your brokerage runs on daily. That estate carries its licensing, hardware refresh, and operational overhead forward every year regardless of volume, and your DOT compliance audit opens in six months — a window in which any migration risk lands directly on the systems examiners will test. Moving load-matching and carrier-settlement onto Google Cloud, using Google Compute Engine for compute and Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL for the data layer, addresses both pressures at once: it replaces a fixed, aging cost base with a platform you can right-size, and it gives you a documented, current infrastructure posture to present when the audit opens — rather than a legacy environment carrying six more months of unmanaged risk.

Over the 2-year, $4,200,000 programme, expect a phased cutover of the 28 SQL Server instances to Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL and the 620 Hyper-V VMs to Compute Engine, sequenced to keep load-matching and settlement operational throughout — [PF-2.14 REVIEW (commitment): confirm the specific cutover sequencing and zero-downtime commitment before this ships, as none has been supplied]. [PF-2.4 GAP: no target run-rate figure or percentage reduction against the $1,850,000 baseline has been supplied — the programme's cost impact should be quantified before this summary is finalized]. [PF-2.4 GAP: no specific DOT compliance control or audit deliverable tied to the migration has been supplied — the audit-readiness claim should name the control it satisfies]. You should expect a governance checkpoint at each phase, a clear line item showing spend against the $4,200,000 programme budget, and a status report timed to land before your audit opens in six months.
